encounters.cc: Burning discomfort in the chest occurring several times per week, particularly after large evening meals

lines: Burning discomfort in the chest occurring several times per week, particularly after large evening meals
He presents to the clinic with a 9-month history of burning discomfort in the chest that occurs several times per week, particularly after large evening meals.
He says the pain sometimes radiates to his throat and is accompanied by a sour, bitter taste in the back of his mouth.
Lying down after dinner or bending forward makes the discomfort worse, while standing or walking after meals seems to help.
He has started sleeping with two pillows at night to reduce the symptoms.
Over the last month, the pain has occasionally awakened him from sleep.
He reports that spicy foods, fried meals, tomato-based sauces, chocolate, and coffee all aggravate his symptoms.
He drinks 2–3 cups of coffee daily, has wine with dinner several nights per week, and eats late at night due to his work schedule.

Past medical history is significant only for seasonal allergic rhinitis.
Medications include occasional over-the-counter antacids, which provide partial but temporary relief.

lines: Intermittent eye redness, itching, and watery discharge for 3 weeks during early summer season
The patient presents for evaluation of recurrent allergic symptoms in the context of known seasonal rhinitis and prior gastroenterology assessment for GERD in January 2020.
He also reports frequent sneezing and a clear nasal discharge, especially when he is outdoors or has the windows open.
These symptoms occur every year around the same time and have been present since his early 30s.
His symptoms are most bothersome in the mornings and when mowing lawns or trimming hedges.
He states that he usually feels better after taking over-the-counter allergy medications such as loratadine or fexofenadine.
These medications relieve his symptoms within an hour.

encounters.cc: Long-standing upper gastrointestinal symptoms with burning sensation behind breastbone

lines: Long-standing upper gastrointestinal symptoms with burning sensation behind breastbone
The patient returns to the Gastroenterology clinic for ongoing management of long-standing upper gastrointestinal symptoms, with similar presentations dating back to January 2020.
He is currently in week 8 of a 12-week course of antiviral therapy for chronic hepatitis C.
He reports experiencing a burning sensation behind his breastbone that worsens after meals and when lying down.
These symptoms have been present for several years and occur multiple times a week, particularly after large meals or consuming coffee or fried foods.
He notes occasional regurgitation of sour-tasting fluid into his mouth but denies dysphagia, odynophagia, vomiting, early satiety, or unintentional weight loss.
He has not had any recent illness or changes in appetite.

encounters.cc: Worsening symptoms of heartburn and regurgitation over the past several weeks despite twice-daily PPI therapy

lines: Worsening symptoms of heartburn and regurgitation over the past several weeks despite twice-daily PPI therapy

The patient returns to the Gastroenterology clinic for follow-up of long-standing gastroesophageal reflux disease, previously evaluated in January 2020 and July 2022 for burning chest discomfort and upper gastrointestinal symptoms.
He reports a several-year history of GERD and has been taking omeprazole twice daily for the last 2 years.

He previously had good symptom control but states that his symptoms flare up during specific times, particularly around holidays or social gatherings when he "eats more than usual." The patient recently attended a multi-day festival where meals were large and frequent, and he noticed that his usual PPI regimen provided little relief.
He asks if his medications should be changed or increased further.

encounters.cc: Worsening fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance over the past 3 weeks with associated shortness of breath and lightheadedness

lines: Worsening fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance over the past 3 weeks with associated shortness of breath and lightheadedness
The patient is a 47-year-old male with gastroesophageal reflux disease (previously evaluated in 2020, 2022, and 2024) who presents to the emergency department.

He has been undergoing treatment for chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and started a new combination therapy 2 months ago, developing increasing shortness of breath when climbing stairs, lightheadedness, and occasional palpitations.
